title: product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The README claims closed generic types from referenced assemblies get no diagnostics from the consumer. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter drops every diagnostic whose location is outside the compilation. Closed generics are routed through GetObjectInfo, whereas [L8] describes non-generic metadata types returning early. This is a new, broader suppression layer than the one recorded. Diagnostics tied to a source member of the consuming type, but with a location in metadata, are silently dropped. That is consistent with [L8]'s intent but not recorded as a general filter. [L10] warns that analyzer reporting changes can cause wrong reports.

title: Receipts/ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1

refutes.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites in TypeCollector.cs (lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff guards only two of them: the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull site (now line 985) and the MemberNeedsKey site (now line 1077). No hunk touches line 735. The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper does not protect that site. The location argument to `Diagnostic.Create` is evaluated before `reportDiagnostic.Invoke`, and in the analyzer path the delegate is non-null. If line 735 is reached for a metadata symbol, the analyzer would still throw IndexOutOfRangeException (AD0001), against the criterion that diagnostics needing a source location must not crash on metadata symbols.

title: Receipts/InheritedMetadataMemberDiagnosticTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 1 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1

refutes.claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper silently drops MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) when a type declared in source inherits public members from a base class in a referenced assembly. Example: `[MessagePackObject] class Derived : Lib.BaseType { [Key(0)] public int X {get;set;} }`, where `Lib.BaseType` has an unkeyed public `int Unkeyed`. The member's location is now null, so the diagnostic is discarded. Before this change the analyzer crashed loudly with AD0001; now the user gets nothing. The remark that the defining compilation reports these problems does not hold here: `BaseType` is not `[MessagePackObject]`, so `Lib` never validates it. L8 only covers types declared in metadata, not source types that inherit from them. The diagnostic should fall back to the derived type's identifier location instead of being dropped.
